column1: # boru Language Specification: Function References (ref / /r)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# ref name   → resolve a function word to its bound Function value WITHOUT
#              invoking it. Companion to the `/r` word-suffix modifier.
# name/r     → the same operation as a suffix (resolve + reference).
# `ref` and `/r` are ONE operation and must behave identically in every
# position. A bare reference is INERT at the reference site: it is left on
# the stack as an (unquoted) Function value and is never auto-invoked —
# not even a 0-arg fn. The SAME value dispatches normally when it is
# re-stepped elsewhere: unwrapped from a paren, retrieved from a map slot,
# or handed to `apply`. References are legal only for function words; a
# non-fn binding raises [boru/illegal_ref] and an unbound name raises
# [boru/undefined_word].
# §1  Bare reference is inert (held) — `ref` ≡ `/r`, no auto-fire
def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  z/r
column3: bare /r holds a 0-arg fn — NOT fired

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  ref z
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  typeof (inc/r)
column3: a held reference is a Function value

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  typeof (ref inc)
# §2  The held value dispatches when RE-STEPPED (paren unwrap)
def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  (z/r)
def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  (ref z)
column3: ref fires when re-stepped — same as /r

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  (inc/r) 5
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  (ref inc) 5
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (sub2/r) 10 3
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (ref sub2) 10 3
# §3  Reference stored in a map slot dispatches via dot-access
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def ops {f: inc/r}  ops.f 5
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def ops {f: (ref inc)}  ops.f 5
column3: ref in a map slot dispatches

column1: # §4  Reference handed to `apply` (stack form: args... fn/r apply)
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  5 inc/r apply
column3: apply invokes a referenced fn against stack args

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  10 3 sub2/r apply
column3: apply on a 2-arg referenced fn (stack order)

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  z/r apply
# §5  Anonymous-function references behave identically
def f ([a:Integer b:Integer] => [a sub b])  typeof (f/r)
def f ([n:Integer] => [n add 1])  (f/r) 5
def f ([n:Integer] => [n add 1])  5 f/r apply

column3: a lambda inside a list is held, never fired in place

column1: # §6  Negatives — reference is legal only for function words
def x 5  x/r
column3: /r on a non-fn binding is rejected

column1: def x 5  ref x
column3: ref on a non-fn binding is rejected

column1: nope/r
ref nope
# §7  A `/r`-marked word feeds forward collection as its REFERENCE
#     value (NUR050 fix): it is not a function-word barrier, so it
#     resolves directly as another word's forward argument. (This
#     retired the historical gotcha where `typeof inc/r` stranded with
#     a signature_error and had to be grouped as `typeof (inc/r)`.)
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  typeof inc/r
column3: bare /r resolves as a forward arg (was the grouping gotcha)

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  typeof (inc/r)
# §8  A fn body's RETURN is delivered, not re-used
#     A frame collapsing to a single Function value hands it back; the
#     frame's own collapse is not a fresh use of it, so it is not invoked
#     there. This is the ParkResult idiom (`ref`'s own mechanism) applied
#     to the frame result, and it is POSITIONAL — nothing is stamped on
#     the value, so the returned reference still dispatches at its next
#     use (§3 map slot, §4 apply both still hold).
#     Before this, `[f/r]` returned the CALL'S RESULT (7) rather than the
#     function — /r silently doing the opposite of what it says.
#     The argument is handed over with `/r` because passing a function as an
#     argument requires it; a bare name is a call.
#     NOT pinned here: what a USER paren does to such a return. `((h z/r))`
#     is an open interpreter/compiler divergence (interp 42, compiled the fn
#     value) — the §2 re-step rule it turns on is itself under revision, so
#     there is no oracle to pin it against, in this corpus or the frontier
#     one. Recorded as NUR073 (Pending) so the gap is not mistaken for
#     coverage; reasoning in design/FUNCTION-VALUE-SCOPE.0.md §12.6. Do not
#     add a row for it until clause 3 is ruled.
def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  def h fn [[f:Function][Any][f/r]]  typeof (h z/r)
column3: a /r'd param returned from a body is the fn, not its result

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  def h fn [[][Any][z/r]]  typeof (h)
column3: same for a module-scope name — not param-specific

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def h fn [[f:Function][Any][f/r]]  typeof (h inc/r)
